rows.final_prompt:
STYLE BALANCE D1:

Use an approximately equal balance between Japanese collectible-card anime illustration and contemporary real-world lifestyle storytelling.

The hobby activity and believable social environment are equally important to the collectible visual energy.

Keep the anime influence clearly visible through:
- linework
- cel shading
- expressive faces
- clean silhouettes
- bright color
- lively gesture
- polished illustrated lighting

But keep people, objects, activities and environments relatively grounded.

Do not exaggerate expressions or poses too far.

Do not turn everyday activities into fantasy scenes.

The intended result is:
“a beautiful real-world lifestyle moment illustrated by a top Japanese commercial anime artist and designed to feel collectible.”

Maintain warmth and natural social interaction.

This version should be the most grounded of D1/D2/D3 while still being unmistakably Japanese-anime illustrated.

Create a premium, original Japanese-inspired collectible hobby illustration for Zync.

This must be clearly illustrated artwork, not photography.

The visual language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial anime illustration and premium collectible-card artwork applied to real-world hobbies.

The image should feel:
- joyful
- colorful
- charming
- energetic
- optimistic
- youthful but not childish
- polished
- iconic
- emotionally inviting
- highly collectible

The hobby subject or central human interaction must feel like the HERO of the illustration.

Do not depict merely an ordinary documentary moment.

Instead depict a memorable “best moment” of doing, discovering, sharing, mastering, enjoying, or becoming excited by the hobby.

Use:
- clean, confident Japanese anime-style linework
- polished cel shading
- soft painted gradients
- crisp subject separation
- expressive faces
- bright, clear eyes
- slightly stylized facial proportions
- stylized but believable anatomy
- elegant simplified forms
- lively natural gestures
- dynamic but readable poses
- strong silhouettes
- intentional hero framing
- colorful, harmonious palettes
- saturated but controlled color
- attractive complementary color relationships
- luminous highlights
- colorful rim-light accents where appropriate
- subtle sparkle or glint accents
- soft environmental particles only when they enhance mood
- expressive environment design
- charming visual details
- graphic shape language
- strong foreground/midground/background separation

The environment must remain believable and relevant to the real-world hobby, but should be interpreted as a beautifully designed anime environment rather than a real photograph.

Simplify reality.

Do not render every tiny real-world detail.

Use selective visual detail and stylization so the image feels drawn and intentionally designed.

The image should have a clear visual hierarchy:
1. hero subject / hero interaction
2. hobby-defining objects or action
3. supporting environment
4. small delightful details

Use subtle heightened visual energy to make the scene collectible.

This may include:
- gentle glowing edge light
- sparkling highlights
- soft color accents
- subtle atmospheric movement
- floating dust/pollen/light flecks
- stylized steam
- wind in clothing/hair
- motion accents
- attractive graphic color shapes

But these effects must NOT transform the hobby into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself calls for fantasy.

The result must remain a real-world hobby scene.

Default emotional direction:

joyful,
optimistic,
curious,
friendly,
energetic,
aspirational,
inviting,
playful,
emotionally alive.

Prefer moments of:
- discovery
- connection
- excitement
- mastery
- friendship
- satisfaction
- surprise
- delight
- fascination

Even serious or intellectual hobbies must feel visually inviting.

For example:

Philosophy should NOT default to:
- gloomy scholars
- sombre brown libraries
- depressing introspection
- dark academic solemnity

Instead it may show:
- animated discussion
- curiosity
- a breakthrough moment
- friends debating ideas
- bright books/notebooks/visual cues
- intellectual excitement

“Knowledge is exciting,” not “knowledge is heavy.”

Legal thriller may be tense, but should still feel visually compelling, stylish and collectible rather than grim or bleak.

Do NOT render:

- real photography
- stock photography
- lifestyle advertising photography
- DSLR realism
- documentary realism
- photojournalism
- cinematic live-action film stills
- photographic skin pores
- photographic depth of field
- real-camera bokeh
- lens artifacts
- camera-real exposure behavior
- photobashing
- Western oil-paint concept art
- gritty Western fantasy concept art
- muted brown editorial palettes
- beige corporate lifestyle advertising
- flat corporate vector illustration
- generic Silicon Valley illustration style
- generic Western magazine editorial art
- New Yorker-style restrained editorial illustration
- dark prestige-TV realism
- gloomy academic illustration
- generic fantasy splash-art chaos
- excessive magic
- battle effects unrelated to the hobby
- glowing supernatural aura
- fantasy weapons or magical relics unless the hobby requires them
- chibi proportions
- preschool cartoon proportions
- hypersexualized anime proportions
- exaggerated fan-service posing
- official TCG UI
- card frames
- white card margins
- decorative collectible-card borders
- HP bars
- stats panels
- attack boxes
- elemental/type icons
- rarity stars
- franchise logos
- recognizable copyrighted characters

IMPORTANT:

The artwork itself must be full-bleed, edge-to-edge illustration.

Do NOT draw a physical card around the artwork.

No border.
No mat.
No card shell.
No rounded white frame.
No decorative frame.
No printed-paper edge.

The application will handle the actual card UI later.

Do not imitate any existing entertainment or collectible-card franchise directly.

commercial-anime polished,

collectible,
